title: What happens to human bodies when they drown?

scenes.title: The Silent Submersion
scenes.narration: Drowning is a rapid and often silent process where the body's airways are submerged in liquid, leading to respiratory failure. It is the third leading cause of unintentional injury death worldwide, claiming over 236,000 lives annually.

scenes.title: The Breath-Holding Reflex
scenes.narration: Upon submersion, the body instinctively holds its breath (apnea), but this is quickly overcome by an overwhelming urge to breathe. Involuntary gasping then causes water to enter the airways, initiating the drowning process.

scenes.title: Laryngospasm & Hypoxia
scenes.narration: Water in the larynx triggers a protective laryngospasm, reflexively closing the vocal cords to prevent further water entry. This blockage, however, also prevents air, leading to rapid hypoxia as oxygen levels in the blood plummet.

scenes.title: Organ Failure Sequence
scenes.narration: As oxygen depletes, the brain suffers first, leading to unconsciousness within 1-2 minutes. The heart, deprived of oxygen, then enters cardiac arrest, typically within 5-10 minutes, causing irreversible organ damage.

scenes.title: Prevention & Response
scenes.narration: Understanding the drowning sequence emphasizes the critical need for prevention, like swimming lessons and supervision, and rapid emergency response. Immediate CPR and medical attention significantly improve survival chances.
